clue.text: If a good Samaritan runs amuck, is this represented?

definitions.text: If a good Samaritan runs amuck, is this represented?

indicators.note: represented means shown in another form, so the gathered letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as part of the letter pool
R is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for runs
taken as written as part of the letter pool
taken as written as part of the letter pool

explanation.surface: A kindly helper who loses control turns a bad situation into a scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runs amuck' looks like the anagram signal, but 'represented' is the signal; runs gives only R and AMUCK is fodder, with IS added at the end. The phrase echoes an old British insurance slogan.
explanation.definitionFit: A rescuer who runs wild overdramatises an emergency, exaggerating a setback into a theatrical fuss.

clue.text: Set on silver plating lasting years

indicators.note: plating is a coat wrapped round something, so the metal's symbol goes round the other pieces

parts.note: AG is the chemical symbol for silver
to gel is to set firm
taken as written

explanation.surface: A setting placed on silver plate that will endure for years.
explanation.walkthrough: The symbol AG splits around GEL + ON, the A in front and the G at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that goes on for ages is long-lasting, enduring over many years.

clue.text: Wanting incentive, time's up unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so these letters fall into a different order

explanation.surface: Someone lacking motivation hears that their allotted time has run out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges the seven letters of TIME'S UP; 'Wanting' is padding to the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Momentum or a driving force is what spurs someone on, just as an incentive does.

clue.text: I don't believe the heart of San Francisco can be this romantic!

parts.note: a goy is a non-Jew, one who doesn't hold the Jewish faith, so a non-believer here

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter, here taken from San

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in disbelief at how romantic a Californian city's centre can be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'San Francisco' reads as one city, but Francisco is the painter's first name: Francisco Goya was a Spanish artist of the Romantic era. GOY is a Yiddish word for a non-Jew.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish painter Francisco de Goya is grouped with Romanticism, so a Francisco can be a Romantic artist.

clue.text: See 1
On time, that fitting finale for Gracie Fields, no less

indicators.note: on is slang for tipsy, so the following word staggers into a new order
the finale is the closing letter of the name Gracie

parts.note: leas are meadows or fields

explanation.surface: A punctual, suitable closing number for the singer Gracie Fields, at the very least.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' scrambles THAT into ATTH; 'finale for' takes E from Gracie. Gracie Fields was a much-loved British singer and comedian, but here Fields gives LEAS; 'fitting' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: At minimum, and not lower than that, is what the phrase means; both say not less.

clue.text: Managed to capture a lunatic fast

indicators.note: to capture is to take inside, so the word for managed holds the other pieces

parts.note: to run something is to manage it, so ran means managed
lunatic and mad both mean insane

explanation.surface: Someone succeeded in catching a madman who was moving quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fast' looks like speed, but it is the noun: the Muslim month of daytime fasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramadan is the Islamic month during which observers abstain from food and drink in daylight, a religious fast.

clue.text: One may demonstrate motorway sign

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in M1
the Archer is Sagittarius, a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: Something might point out what a motorway sign shows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sign' looks like a road sign but means a star sign: Sagittarius, the Archer.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone on a protest march is a demonstrator, taking part in a public rally.

clue.text: No way Jose, international chef, wins hearts a lot for preparation

indicators.note: preparation means making something ready, as a chef works ingredients over, so the letters get reworked

parts.note: taken as written as part of the letter pool
taken as written as part of the letter pool
H is the abbreviation for hearts in card games
taken as written as part of the letter pool

explanation.surface: A globetrotting cook flatly refuses, though he charms many people with his cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for preparation' rearranges INTERNATIONAL, CHEF, H and A LOT; 'wins' serves only the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are emphatic refusals; the idiom says nothing could tempt you, however great the reward.

clue.text: See 8
To excessively reward old man's nothing particularly enthralling

parts.note: O looks like zero, meaning nothing

indicators.note: enthralling means holding captive, so one word is held inside the other

parts.note: very and particularly both intensify, as in very good
pa is an informal word for father, one's old man

explanation.surface: A father's nothing special that captivates, offered as an overgenerous payment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enthralling' looks like an adjective meaning gripping, but here it means holding captive. 'old man' is a familiar way to say father.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying more than something is worth means rewarding someone too generously.

clue.text: Light umbrella covering manure-supplier

indicators.note: covering means one thing lies over another, so the letters sit concealed within these two words

explanation.surface: A lightweight umbrella shelters a farmhand spreading manure.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'Light umbrella'. A tumbrel was a farm cart, often for dung, later used to carry prisoners to the guillotine.
explanation.definitionFit: A tumbrel was a two-wheeled tipping cart used for carrying dung onto fields.

clue.text: Sort of reception delayed wedding guest might receive from The Rime

definitions.text: Sort of reception delayed wedding guest might receive from The Rime

parts.words: Sort of reception delayed wedding guest might receive from The Rime
parts.note: a reception can be a cold, unfriendly welcome; in Coleridge's poem the Ancient Mariner holds up a Wedding-Guest, and rime is also hoar frost

explanation.surface: A late wedding guest gets a chilly welcome, with a nod to Coleridge's poem.
explanation.walkthrough: In The Rime of the Ancient Mariner, the Mariner detains a Wedding-Guest; rime also means hoar frost, so something from The Rime is frozen.
explanation.definitionFit: A cold, unfriendly welcome is described with the adjective for icy weather.

clue.text: ID pic for which rash folk have repaired parts

indicators.note: the two parts of the word have been put back in another order, so the front section moves to the back

parts.note: hotheads are impetuous, rash people

explanation.surface: An identity photo for reckless people who have patched themselves up.
explanation.walkthrough: HOT moves from the front of HOTHEADS to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A photograph of the face, as on an identity card, is called a headshot.

clue.text: See 8
Tender point argued before dissecting bloody dogfish

indicators.note: dissecting means cutting into, so the inner pieces cut open the word for bloody

parts.note: red is the colour of blood, so bloody
the gist is the main point of an argument
ere is an old word for before
a nurse, or nursehound, is a kind of dogfish

explanation.surface: A tender point is argued before someone cuts up a bloody dogfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dissecting' splits the word for bloody between its E and D. 'Tender' looks like an adjective, but it is a noun, one who tends; the dogfish called a nurse closes the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A nurse is someone who tends the sick, so a carer or tender.

clue.text: Energy over time

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy
on and over can both mean resting above, as in a lid on or over a jar

explanation.surface: Energy expended across a span of time.
explanation.definitionFit: An age is a vast span of history, an immeasurably long period.

clue.text: Long runner is winding round top of knoll

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the turned word goes round a letter
winding means turning back on itself, so the little word is read backwards
the top of a word is its first letter, here from knoll

explanation.surface: A long-distance runner winds around the summit of a small hill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winding' turns IS into SI, which goes 'round' K, the first letter of knoll.
explanation.definitionFit: Each of a pair of long narrow runners strapped to boots for gliding over snow.

clue.text: Stimulant with nasty borosilicate added in

indicators.note: nasty suggests something gone bad, so these letters are scrambled

parts.note: and can mean with, as in bread and butter
taken as written as part of the letter pool

explanation.surface: A drug laced with harmful heat-resistant glass compound.
explanation.walkthrough: BOROSILICATE is rearranged with AND (from 'with'), which 'added in' says is put into the mix. Borosilicate is the heat-proof glass used in lab and oven ware.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscle-building synthetic hormones work by stimulating tissue growth, hence the description as a stimulant.

clue.text: One who booked Meg, Jo, Amy and Beth sent off England winger

definitions.text: One who booked Meg, Jo, Amy and Beth

indicators.note: sent off is read as sent away from the front, so the first letter of the footballer's name is dropped

parts.note: Theo Walcott was a winger for England's football team

explanation.surface: A referee who cautioned four girls dismissed an England wide man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'booked' and 'sent off' read as a referee's actions, but 'booked' means put into a book: Louisa May Alcott wrote Little Women, whose sisters are Meg, Jo, Amy and Beth.
explanation.definitionFit: The American novelist Louisa May Alcott wrote about the four March sisters in Little Women.

clue.text: 80s act portraying art master in a war film

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the others, between the A and the film title

parts.note: Zulu is a 1964 film about the battle of Rorke's Drift
MA is a Master of Arts degree

explanation.surface: A performer playing an art teacher in a war movie.
explanation.walkthrough: Amazulu were a British reggae-pop band of the 1980s; 'portraying' is only a link. Zulu (1964) is a well-known British film about a colonial battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Amazulu were a pop group who had chart hits in the 1980s, so a musical act of that decade.

clue.text: Aromatic plant princess used to stuff duck repeatedly

indicators.note: a stuffing goes inside, so the princess's name fills the doubled letter
repeatedly says the letter is written twice

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nought, written O
Regan is one of King Lear's daughters, a princess in Shakespeare

explanation.surface: A fragrant herb that a princess keeps using to stuff a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' suggests cooking, but it is the cricket nought O, doubled by 'repeatedly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregano is a fragrant culinary herb, wild marjoram.

clue.text: Educated man fed fine crackers

indicators.note: crackers means crazy, so these letters go wild into a new order

explanation.surface: A learned man gave out fine biscuits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crackers' looks like biscuits for feeding, but it is the slang for mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Effendi is a Turkish title of respect for a learned or educated gentleman.

clue.text: Folding a cheque up on way out of London?

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the road follows
in a down clue up means read from the bottom, so these letters run backwards

parts.note: a giro is a payment cheque, especially a British benefit cheque
the M1 motorway runs north out of London, written MI

explanation.surface: A cheque folded and pocketed while driving out of the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses A GIRO to give ORIGA. The M1 is Britain's main motorway north from London, with the figure 1 read as I.
explanation.definitionFit: Origami is the Japanese art of paper folding.

clue.text: German chap counting the calories?

definitions.meaning: A common German male first name
one who watches what they eat to lose weight

explanation.definitionFit: A common German forename for a man; also someone on a slimming regime.

clue.text: Fellow porter possibly clutching top-left key for fuse

parts.note: co- means fellow or joint, as in co-worker

indicators.note: clutching means holding tight, so the beer word holds the key inside

parts.note: porter is a dark beer, an example of ale
Esc, the escape key, sits at the top left of a keyboard

explanation.surface: A fellow luggage porter grasping the upper-left key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'porter' suggests a carrier, but it is the dark beer; the 'possibly' says it is one example of ALE.
explanation.definitionFit: To merge into one mass is to join together, as metals fuse.

clue.text: No longer in solitary workplace?

parts.note: off means not on duty or no longer in play
ice suggests cold isolation, solitary confinement being known as the cooler

explanation.surface: Someone released from solitary confinement goes back to work.
explanation.walkthrough: Being 'on ice' or in 'the cooler' suggests isolation; coming off it gives OFF ICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A room or building where people do desk work.

clue.text: Short description — of monocle?

definitions.meaning: a shortened specification, a brief listing of details
a single eyeglass is a lone half of a pair of glasses

explanation.definitionFit: Spec abbreviates specification; spectacles are specs, so one lens is jokingly a single spec.

clue.text: It's gloved hand that is returning wave?

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the assembled letters are read backwards
gloved means wrapped round like a glove on a hand, so the word for it surrounds the other

parts.note: taken as written, the possessive adding no letter
manus is Latin for hand, also the anatomical term

explanation.surface: A glove-covered hand is waving back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gloved' puts the Latin hand inside IT, making IMANUST, and 'returning' turns that round; 'that is' only links. The apostrophe-s of It's adds no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsunami is a huge sea wave caused by an undersea earthquake.

clue.text: "His nibs" George Eliot?

parts.note: nibs are pen tips, so a writer's nibs suggest a pen; George Eliot was the male byline used by the novelist Mary Ann Evans

explanation.surface: A self-important man named George Eliot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'His nibs' is British slang for a self-important person, but here nibs are pen points; George Eliot was Mary Ann Evans's writing name.
explanation.definitionFit: George Eliot was the pseudonym under which Mary Ann Evans published her novels.
